entry.title: Hansen–Vukicevic's conjecture for commuting and non-commuting graphs of finite groups
entry.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite non-abelian group, and let $\Gamma(G)$ denote either the commuting graph or the non-commuting graph of $G$. Its first and second Zagreb indices are

$$
M_{1}(\Gamma(G))=\sum_{v\in v(\Gamma(G))}\deg(v)^2,\qquad M_{2}(\Gamma(G))=\sum_{uv\in e(\Gamma(G))}\deg(u)\deg(v).
$$

**Hansen–Vuki\v{c}evi\'{c}'s conjecture for group graphs.**

$$
\frac{M_{2}(\Gamma(G))}{|e(\Gamma(G))|}\geq\frac{M_{1}(\Gamma(G))}{|v(\Gamma(G))|}.
$$

The authors report computational verification for commuting and non-commuting graphs of finite non-abelian groups of order at most $1000$. The conjecture remains open in the supplied text.

entry.title: Hansen–Johnsen–Ranestad conjecture on higher weights of Grassmann codes
entry.literal_statement: Let $G(l,m)$ be the Grassmann variety of $l$-dimensional subspaces of an $m$-dimensional vector space over ${\mathbb F}_q$, embedded in the Plücker projective space $\mathbf P^{k-1}$, where $k=\binom{m}{l}$. Let $d_i$ be the higher weights of the Grassmann code $C(l,m)$, and let $J_i$ be the maximal number of ${\mathbb F}_q$-rational points of $G(l,m)$ lying on a codimension $i$ linear subspace of the Plücker space. A **Schubert union** is a union of Schubert varieties in $G(l,m)$. **Hansen–Johnsen–Ranestad's conjecture.** The higher weights of the Grassmann codes $G(l,m)$ are always computed by Schubert unions: for every $i$, there is a codimension $i$ linear subspace whose intersection with $G(l,m)$ is a Schubert union containing $J_i$ ${\mathbb F}_q$-rational points, and hence $d_i=n-J_i$. The conjecture predicts that Schubert unions suffice to attain the maxima governing all higher weights; the paper's stated goal is to confirm it in the case $l=2$, while the general assertion is presented as the conjecture from the cited work.

entry.title: Aouchiche–Hansen–Zheng conjecture on the Randić index and matching number

literal_record.title: Aouchiche–Hansen–Zheng conjecture on the Randić index and matching number
literal_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices, where $n\ge 3$. Write $R(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}(d(u)d(v))^{-1/2}$ for its Randić index and let $\alpha'(G)$ denote its matching number. Define

$$
p=\left\lfloor\frac{n+4}{7}\right\rfloor,\qquad q=\left\lfloor\frac{6n+2}{7}\right\rfloor.
$$

**Aouchiche–Hansen–Zheng conjecture.** One has

$$
R(G)-\alpha'(G)\le\sqrt{\left\lfloor\frac{n+4}{7}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{6n+2}{7}\right\rfloor}-\left\lfloor\frac{n+4}{7}\right\rfloor,
$$

with equality if and only if $G=K_{p,q}$.

The conjecture proposes the extremal connected graph for the difference between the Randić index and matching number. It was disproved by the existence of a counterexample; the corresponding restricted extremal problem for subcubic graphs was solved by Du, Hu, and collaborators.
literal_record.source_name: Pei Liu, Feiyu Nan, Suil O and Ruiling Zheng, “A sharp Randić bound for König–Egerváry graphs and a conjecture of Aouchiche, Hansen, and Zheng”, arXiv:2607.23918 (2026).
literal_record.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2009–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1607.08258](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.08258), [arXiv:1104.0426](https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.0426), [arXiv:0906.5230](https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.5230).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23918

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of July 2026). “The analogous extremal problem restricted to subcubic graphs was recently solved by Du, Hu, and three of the present authors , where the existence of a counterexample to Conjecture was first announced.”

entry.ordinary_attempts: Source supplies complete-bipartite counterexamples to the conjectured floor extremizer, via maximizing sqrt(s(n-s))-s and a Pell construction. Both versions include the strict comparison. The literal record also says disproved.

entry.title: Hansen's Szeged–Wiener index conjecture for bipartite graphs
entry.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite, simple, connected bipartite graph with $n \geq 4$ vertices and $m \geq n$ edges. Its Wiener index is

$$
W(G)=\sum_{\{u,v\}\subseteq V(G)}d(u,v),
$$

and its Szeged index is

$$
Sz(G)=\sum_{e=uv\in E(G)}n_u(e)n_v(e),
$$

where $n_u(e)$ and $n_v(e)$ count the vertices closer to $u$ and $v$, respectively, for the edge $e=uv$. **Hansen's conjecture.**

$$
Sz(G)-W(G)\geq 4n-8.
$$

The bound is best possible: equality is attained by a graph formed from a $4$-cycle $C_4$ and a tree $T$ on $n-3$ vertices sharing one vertex. The conjecture concerns a lower bound relating two classical graph indices and, in the stated source, no resolution is supplied.
entry.actual_review_depth: Source Theorem 2.2 and full proof, Lemma 2.1 full proof, Corollary 2.3 read in latest single arXiv version.
entry.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_scope: Theorem 2.2 has exactly finite simple connected bipartite n>=4,m>=n hypotheses and conclusion Sz-W>=4n-8. It decomposes into blocks after proving the two-connected case via pair contributions. Equality example also matches literally.
entry.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: The source itself solves the assigned conjecture. Independent repair or formalization would not be a new outcome. Separate 1104.2122 companion and final journal body not fully read.

entry.title: The monotonicity conjecture for polychromatic 2-regular subgraphs

full_literal_record.title: The monotonicity conjecture for polychromatic 2-regular subgraphs
full_literal_record.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices. A subgraph is **2-regular** if every vertex has degree $2$. An edge-coloring of $K_n$ is called polychromatic for a family of subgraphs when every subgraph in the family receives all colors used by the coloring.

**Monotonicity conjecture.** Let $n\geq 6$ and let $j$ be an integer such that $3\leq j<n$; if $j=5$, assume $n\geq 9$. If an edge-coloring $\varphi$ of $K_n$ has the property that every 2-regular subgraph spanning $j$ vertices gets all colors, then every 2-regular subgraph spanning at least $j$ vertices gets all colors under $\varphi$.

The conjecture extends the authors' results for cycles to 2-regular graphs. It is presented as an expected analogue of a proved cycle theorem, with possible exceptions only in small cases; the supplied text gives no resolution.
full_literal_record.source_name: John Goldwasser and Ryan Hansen, “Polychromatic colorings of 1-regular and 2-regular subgraphs of complete graphs”, arXiv:2009.08960 (2020).
full_literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.08960

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2020).

entry.title: Li et al.'s log-concavity conjecture for Clar covering polynomials

full_record.title: Li et al.'s log-concavity conjecture for Clar covering polynomials
full_record.statement:
Let $H$ be a hexagonal system, meaning a 2-connected finite plane graph whose interior faces are regular hexagons of side length one. Let $\zeta(H,x)$ be the Clar covering polynomial of $H$.

**Li et al.'s conjecture.** The polynomial $\zeta(H,x)$ is log-concave.

Since the coefficients of $\zeta(H,x)$ are positive, this is stronger than the unimodality conjecture for Clar covering polynomials. The conjecture was proposed after extensive numerical testing and remains open in the supplied source.
full_record.source_name: Yan-Ting Xie, Yong-De Feng and Shou-Jun Xu, “A relation between the cube polynomials of partial cubes and the clique polynomials of their crossing graphs”, arXiv:2303.14671 (2024).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.14671

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2023). “Although Conjecture associated with median graphs is false, the conjecture on the resonance graphs of hexagonal systems (a subclass of median graphs) is still open.”

entry.assessment_and_gap: Conjecture5.2 concerns actual hexagonal-system resonance graphs. Examples4.1–4.2 disprove only median-graph generalizations. Pendant cube constructions lack a hexagonal resonance realizability bridge. Related r244 unimodality hold remains relevant; not cleared.

entry.title: Šoltés graph uniqueness conjecture
entry.literal_statement: Let $C_{11}$ denote the cycle on eleven vertices. A **Šoltés graph** is a graph for which deleting any vertex leaves the Wiener index unchanged. **Šoltés graph uniqueness conjecture.** The cycle on eleven vertices, $C_{11}$, is the only Šoltés graph. The source notes that this is reinforced by the absence of Šoltés graphs among vertex-transitive graphs with fewer than $48$ vertices, but gives no resolution.

entry.title: Harcos–Soltész conjecture on $K_{2,4}$-creating Hamilton paths
entry.literal_statement:
For a graph $G$, let $H_n(G)$ be the maximum number of Hamilton paths in $K_n$ such that the union of any two contains $G$ as a subgraph. In particular, $H_n(K_{2,4})$ is the corresponding maximum for the complete bipartite graph $K_{2,4}$.

**Harcos–Soltész conjecture.** There is a constant $C>0$ such that

$$
H_n(K_{2,4})\le C^n.
$$

The conjecture is equivalent to the reversing permutations conjecture. It would substantially improve the paper's upper bound, which is only of order $n^{n/2+o(n)}$ up to an exponential factor.
entry.source_name: John Byrne and Michael Tait, “Improved upper bounds on even-cycle creating Hamilton paths”, arXiv:2304.02164 (2023).

record.title: Random-current phase transition conjecture on the hexagonal lattice
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{H}$ be the hexagonal lattice. Denote by $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{H}}$ the single random-current measure and by $\phi_{\mathbb{H}}$ the associated random-cluster model.

**Hexagonal-lattice random-current conjecture.** All phase transitions of the random current and random-cluster model on the hexagonal lattice coincide:

$$
\beta_c^{\operatorname{perc}}(\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{H}})=\beta_c(\phi_{\mathbb{H}}).
$$

The loop $\mathrm{O}(1)$ model has an explicitly understood phase diagram on the hexagonal lattice, whereas the random-current measure is expected to exhibit a more generic behaviour. The conjectured equality remains open in the source.

entry.title: Odd-minor Duchet–Meyniel conjecture of Ji, Song, Weiss, and Zhang
entry.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, let $\alpha(G)$ denote its independence number, and let $oh(G)$ be the largest integer $\ell$ such that $G$ has an odd $K_\ell$ minor.

**Odd-minor Duchet–Meyniel conjecture.** For any graph $G$ of order $n$,

$$
oh(G)\geq \left\lceil\frac{n}{\alpha(G)}\right\rceil.
$$

This is the odd-minor analogue of the Duchet–Meyniel conjecture and is stronger than the corresponding lower bound obtained by replacing $oh(G)$ with the ordinary minor parameter. The source does not state whether it has been resolved.

entry.title: Jovović–Koledin–Stanić spectral-gap conjecture for trees
entry.statement: Let $\mathcal{T}(n)$ be the family of trees on $n$ vertices. For a tree, write $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ for its two largest adjacency eigenvalues, and let $DC(k,k,\ell)$ denote a double comet with two equal pendant-path lengths $k$ and central path length $\ell$, where $2k+\ell=n$. **Jovović–Koledin–Stanić conjecture.** In $\mathcal{T}(n)$, the spectral gap $\lambda_1-\lambda_2$ is minimized by a double comet $DC(k,k,\ell)$ such that $2k+\ell=n$. The conjecture concerns the extremal structure of the spectral gap among trees and is part of the broader study of combinations of the first two eigenvalues. The supplied context gives no resolution, so its status remains open.

entry.title: DeLaViña–Waller conjecture on the Wiener index of graphs of order $2d+1$
entry.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite connected graph, let $d$ be its diameter, let $W(G)$ denote its Wiener index, and let $C_{2d+1}$ denote the cycle on $2d+1$ vertices. **DeLaViña–Waller conjecture.** If

$$
d\geq 3\quad\text{and}\quad |V(G)|=2d+1,
$$

then

$$
W(G)\leq W(C_{2d+1}).
$$

The conjecture concerns the maximum Wiener index among graphs with prescribed diameter and order. The paper states that it proves the conjecture for relevant classes involving $0,1,2,3$ or $n-4$ cut vertices, while the general problem remains unresolved.

entry.title: Aouchiche–Hansen conjecture on the second adjacency eigenvalue
entry.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices, with $m$ edges, clique number $\omega$, and second largest adjacency eigenvalue $\rho_2$.

**Aouchiche–Hansen conjecture.** The following assertions hold:

- If $n$ is odd, then $|\rho_2|\,\omega\leq m-2$, with equality if and only if $G$ is composed of $K_{(n+1)/2}$ and $K_{(n-1)/2}$ linked by an edge, or $K_{(n-1)/2}$ and $K_{(n-1)/2}$ linked by a path.
- If $n$ is even, then $|\rho_2|\,\omega-m$ is maximized if and only if $G$ is composed of two copies of $K_{n/2}$ linked by an edge.

The conjecture strengthens an earlier bound $|\rho_2(G)|\leq m/\omega$ for graphs other than $K_2$. The source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

entry.title: Sedlar–Škrekovski's mixed metric dimension conjecture
entry.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph that is not a cycle. Write $O(G)=V(G)\cup E(G)$, let $\operatorname{dim_m}(G)$ denote the minimum cardinality of a mixed metric generator of $G$, let $\ell(G)$ be the number of leaves of $G$, and let

$$
c(G)=|E(G)|-|V(G)|+1
$$

be its cyclomatic number. **Sedlar–Škrekovski's conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{dim_m}(G)\leq \ell(G)+2c(G).
$$

Sedlar and Škrekovski proposed this bound after determining the mixed metric dimension of unicyclic graphs. The conjecture concerns the mixed metric dimension of connected graphs beyond cycles; its resolution is not established in the supplied source.

entry.title: Butterfly trace conjecture

actual_disposition.title: Butterfly trace conjecture
actual_disposition.statement:
Let $B$ be the butterfly poset on four elements $a,b,c,d$, with $a,b<_B c,d$. For a family $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$, let $Tr_{n-1}(n,B)$ denote the maximum size of a family whose traces on all $(n-1)$-subsets contain no copy of $B$. **Butterfly trace conjecture.** If $n\geq 5$, then

$$
Tr_{n-1}(n,B)=\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}.
$$

The paper proves the related exact formula $Tr(n,B)=\lfloor 3n/2\rfloor+1$, but the asserted value for traces on $(n-1)$-subsets is posed as an open problem.
actual_disposition.source_name: Dániel Gerbner, Balázs Patkós and Máté Vizer, “Forbidden subposet problems for traces of set families”, arXiv:1706.01212 (2017).
actual_disposition.reason: Must forbid butterfly copies in every (n-1)-trace for every n>=5. The distinct Tr(n,B) formula does not settle this. No short compression/injection or structural obstruction is source-qualified.
